> 「初日分以恒河沙等身布施，中日分复以恒河沙等身布施，后日分亦以恒河沙等身布施，如是无量百千万亿劫以身布施；若复有人，闻此经典，信心不逆，其福胜彼。」

Section fifteen takes the comparison to a place where no further escalation is possible.

Morning, noon, and evening: bodies equal in number to the sands of the Ganges, given away. Not once, but for 百千万亿劫 — an unconceivable span of aeons. The giving of life, repeated without pause, forever.

And then: a person who hears this sutra and whose mind does not oppose it is more fortunate than that.

## 信心不逆

不逆 — not opposing, not resisting, not turning against. The bar is lower than "believes" and higher than it sounds.

It means the sentence is allowed in. No immediate flinch, no argument mounted before the words land, no automatic defence of the position one already holds. The mind does not push back.

This is a specific and testable capacity, and most readers fail it on the first pass without noticing: they read, understand the words, and simultaneously file them under a category that neutralises them — "mystical", "Eastern", "already familiar".

## 荷担如来

The person who receives, holds, reads, and explains this is said to 荷担 — to carry on the shoulder — the awakening of the Tathāgata.

The image is of physical labour: a weight taken up and moved. Not a title conferred, not a diploma issued. The teaching is transported by people who carry it, and that is all the transmission there has ever been.

Which is why the section's escalation is not absurd. If the only thing that keeps a view like this alive across centuries is someone carrying it, then carrying it outweighs any quantity of treasure — because treasure, however vast, cannot carry anything.

## 为发大乘者说

The sutra states its audience: for those who have aroused the greater vehicle, and for those who have aroused the highest vehicle.

大乘 here is defined by scope of intention — liberation aimed at all beings, not only oneself. 最上乘 by directness — the view that does not stop at any rung of the ladder.

## 乐小法者

The section then says something unflattering: those who delight in the smaller teaching cannot hear this, cannot receive it, cannot ask about it.

Read as sectarian ranking, this is ugly. The book reads it as diagnosis: a mind content with its own liberation has no room for a teaching that dismantles the position of the one who is being liberated. The limitation is structural, not moral. It is not that such practitioners are bad; it is that the furniture is already full.

## 不可思议、不可称量

The merits are called unthinkable, unweighable, boundless.

Not "very large" — that would still be inside the scale. Outside the scale means: no exchange rate exists, so no calculation can be made, so no bargain can be struck.

The book flags the popular inversion: treating "inconceivable merit" as a guarantee that wishes get granted. That converts the unmeasurable back into a currency, which is precisely what the phrase excludes.

## The test

Read the sentence *do not abide anywhere* — slowly, once.

Then notice what happened in the second after it. Was there a small movement of resistance, of reclassification, of "yes but"?

If there was, you have met 逆. The section's whole claim is that removing that small movement is worth more than every body given away for aeons — and it is worth more because it is the only thing that changes what you are.
